comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation issues structured liabilities linked to various financial variables, valuing them using quantitative models that incorporate observable and unobservable inputs, including the Corporation's own credit spread determined by secondary bond market references.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC incorporate their own credit spreads into the valuation of liabilities under the fair value option using observable secondary bond market data. Citi specifically applies this to its own debt valuation adjustments (DVA) on elected liabilities, with changes reflected in AOCI. Similarly, BAC uses its own credit spread, determined by reference to observable secondary bond market spreads, to determine the discount rate for valuing structured liabilities under the fair value option.

sentences.text: Own debt valuation adjustments are recognized on Citi's liabilities for which the fair value option has been elected using Citi's credit spreads observed in the bond market.
Changes in fair value of fair value option liabilities related to changes in Citigroup's own credit spreads (DVA) are reflected as a component of AOCI.
The Corporation also considers the impact of its own credit spread in determining the discount rate used to value these liabilities.
The credit spread is determined by reference to observable spreads in the secondary bond market.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm calculates the fair value of financial liabilities subject to the fair value option by discounting future cash flows at a rate that incorporates the firm's credit spreads.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs calculate the fair value of financial liabilities subject to the fair value option by incorporating their own credit spreads. Citi uses observed bond market credit spreads to estimate changes in fair value resulting from instrument-specific credit risk. Goldman Sachs calculates fair value by discounting future cash flows at a rate that incorporates the firm's credit spreads. While GS also details the materiality of losses on loans (gs_2024_8_D278), the core methodology for liabilities aligns with Citi's DVA approach.

sentences.text: Changes in fair value resulting from changes in instrument-specific credit risk were estimated by incorporating the Company's current credit spreads observable in the bond market into the relevant valuation technique used to value each liability as described above.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation adjustments on fair value option elected liabilities and DVA
comparisons.peer_summary: Valuation of liabilities under the fair value option accounts for the Firm's own credit risk, specifically through Debit Valuation Adjustment (DVA) which reflects changes in the probability of default and loss given default based on credit spread movements. Realized DVA gains or losses are recognized in principal transactions revenue, while unrealized amounts are reported in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI).
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan explicitly link DVA on fair value option elected liabilities to changes in the firm's credit spread observed in the bond market. Citi recognizes DVA changes in AOCI, while JPMorgan reports unrealized DVA gains/losses in OCI and realized gains/losses in principal transactions revenue. Both use bond market observations to estimate changes in probability of default and loss given default (JPM) or instrument-specific credit risk (Citi).

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm applies credit-related valuation adjustments to Borrowings for which the fair value option was elected and to OTC derivatives, considering the impact of changes in its own credit spreads based on secondary bond market observations.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley apply credit-related valuation adjustments to Borrowings for which the fair value option was elected, considering the impact of changes in their own credit spreads based on observations of secondary bond market spreads. This mirrors Citi's practice of recognizing own debt valuation adjustments using Citi's credit spreads observed in the bond market.
